title: Grateful Dead Live at NY State Pavilion, Flushing Meadow Park on 1969-07-11
venue: NY State Pavilion, Flushing Meadow Park
lineage: SBD MC > C  > D > CD + patch from AUD master > low-gen reel > cassette > CD > SHN

ai_review.summary: A mostly soundboard tape with hiss and occasional drop‑outs, but a smoking 1969 show – Hard to Handle on pedal steel, an all‑out Alligator jam and stellar Dupree’s make it shine.
ai_review.review: This recording captures the raw energy of a July 1969 Dead night.  Despite hissy tape quality, early audience‑mic drums and some cuts (notably in Lovelight), the board mix is surprisingly clear for the era and lets listeners hear Jerry Garcia on pedal steel, a powerful Hard to Handle, an epic Alligator>Other One sequence and one of the best early‑era Dupree’s.  The performance is consistently high‑energy with several standout moments that outweigh the technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (high energy, standout songs) while noting modest but acceptable tape issues; weighted combination yields a solid 4.2‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally board mix with occasional hiss and drop‑outs; first minutes of drums are audience mono, then switches to stereo board. Lovelight is clipped on this release. Overall decent clarity for a 1969 tape but not pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows with a strong early drive, a memorable Alligator jam that segues into The Other One, and a high‑octane second half highlighted by Dupree's and High Time. Even where cuts occur the musical momentum stays intact.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pedal steel on Hard to Handle and Dire Wolf; described as joyfully melodic and a highlight of the night.
band_member_comments.Phil: Sings on Momma Tried; occasional bass presence noted, but no specific 'bomb' comments.
band_member_comments.Bob: Opening jokes are called “priceless” by one reviewer.
band_member_comments.Drums: Multiple reviewers praise the drum sound as fantastic and a key driver of the Dupree's performance.
